title: Lena and the Vow
premise: Marine biologist Xanthe Voss has spent ten years on a remote island counting sea turtles and avoiding her past, comforted by anonymous letters from a stranger who signed only 'V.' When the letter writer — her childhood best friend turned estranged first love, Rowan Ashe — buys the cottage next door, Xanthe discovers the letters were never anonymous at all, and that Rowan has been quietly paying off the debt that destroyed her family. As the last ferry of the season approaches, Xanthe must choose between exposing Rowan's deception to protect the island's turtle sanctuary or forgiving them and herself for a decade of silence. She chooses truth over loyalty to her own bitterness, confessing her own buried betrayal first, and they board the ferry together as partners in saving the sanctuary.
about_author: Hazel Dunmore is a former tide-pool docent who writes love stories set where the land runs out of road. She lives on a windswept peninsula with an aging dog named Buoy.

chapters.title: The Count
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Opening with dawn turtle counts, we learn she measures time in nests, not years, and that a decade of unsigned letters sits in a shoebox under her bed. Emotional beat: guarded contentment about to crack.

chapters.title: A Moving Truck in October
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. A stranger unloads boxes into the long-empty cottage next door; she recognizes Rowan Ashe instantly and hides behind her dune fence like a coward. Beat: panic disguised as irritation.

chapters.title: Letters, Unsigned
chapters.summary: Rowan's POV. Rowan unpacks the carbon copies of ten years of letters, revealing they wrote every one but never signed, believing Xanthe knew. Beat: tender, terrible hope.

chapters.title: Tide Charts and Small Talk
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Forced proximity at the dock: Rowan asks about the turtle season with suspicious fluency in her life's details. She notices, files it away, says nothing. Beat: suspicion blooming under politeness.

chapters.title: What the Storm Took
chapters.summary: Dual POV flashback. Ten years ago: the Voss family's marina failed, Xanthe blamed Rowan's father, and Rowan left without a word. Beat: the wound shown whole for the first time.

chapters.title: Nest Nine
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. A storm threatens a late nest; Rowan shows up unasked and works through the night beside her. Wet, exhausted, almost laughing together. Beat: the first thaw.

chapters.title: The Debt
chapters.summary: Rowan's POV. We learn Rowan has spent a decade anonymously repaying the loan shark who ruined the Voss family — money earned by working for the very development company now eyeing the island. Beat: guilt compounding.

chapters.title: Harbor Meeting
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. The town council announces a resort proposal that would pave the nesting beach; Rowan speaks against it, stunning the room. Beat: allies before either admits it.

chapters.title: Coffee, Almost Honest
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. First real conversation in ten years; both circle the letters, neither lands. Xanthe quotes a line back to Rowan without realizing whose it is. Beat: intimacy rekindling dangerously.

chapters.title: Carbon Paper
chapters.summary: Rowan's POV. Rowan nearly confesses everything over coffee, then sees the old hatred in Xanthe's eyes when her father's name comes up, and swallows it. Beat: cowardice dressed as kindness.

chapters.title: The Petition
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Xanthe and Rowan campaign door to door against the resort; the island rallies. Working side by side feels like being twenty again. Beat: falling, unwillingly.

chapters.title: First Kiss, Last Ferry Season
chapters.summary: Rowan's POV. After a victory at the county hearing, they kiss on the cold beach. Joy — immediately shadowed by everything unsaid. Beat: peak sweetness before the fall.

chapters.title: The Ledger
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Xanthe finds a bank ledger in Rowan's cottage showing payments to the man who ruined her family — and reads it as proof Rowan was complicit all along. Beat: betrayal misread.

chapters.title: Accusation at Low Tide
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Xanthe confronts Rowan publicly; Rowan, humiliated, refuses to explain, protecting a promise made to Xanthe's dying father. Beat: the rupture.

chapters.title: Silence, Again
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Days of frozen silence; Xanthe rereads the letters and begins noticing what she missed — references only someone present at her worst moments could know. Beat: doubt creeping in.

chapters.title: Her Father's Tape
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Among her father's effects, Xanthe finds a voicemail he saved: him thanking 'young Ashe' for taking on his debts, asking Rowan never to tell her. Beat: the ground shifting.

chapters.title: What I Did
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV, confessional. Xanthe faces her own secret: it was she who tipped off the loan shark about the marina's accounts, trusting him over everyone, causing the ruin she blamed on others. Beat: the person in the mirror.

chapters.title: Confrontation in the Dunes
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Xanthe goes to Rowan not for an apology but to give one; Rowan finally tells the whole truth about the letters and the debt. Anger, grief, then something quieter. Beat: mutual reckoning.

chapters.title: The Resort Strikes Back
chapters.summary: Rowan's POV. The developer reveals Rowan's old employment and uses it to discredit the petition; the town turns. Rowan considers leaving on the last ferry to save Xanthe's reputation. Beat: sacrifice offered.

chapters.title: Council Chamber
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. At the final vote, Xanthe stands and tells the whole town her own role in her family's ruin, spending her credibility to vouch for Rowan's decade of restitution. Beat: climax — truth chosen over self-protection.

chapters.title: Last Ferry
chapters.summary: Dual POV. The vote passes; the sanctuary survives. At the dock, Xanthe asks Rowan to stay not out of debt but choice; Rowan tears up the return ticket. Beat: release.

chapters.title: Signed, Finally
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV, epilogue. Spring nesting season: Rowan signs their name to a new letter — an invitation, a home, a future — and slides it under a door that no longer locks between them. Beat: peace earned.
